sources.entry: Platypus - Mac developer tool that creates application bundles from command line scripts.

summary.one_liner: Platypus is a macOS developer tool that wraps command line scripts (shell, Python, Perl, Ruby, and others) into native Mac application bundles.
summary.what_it_does: Platypus wraps a script in an application bundle together with a slim native app binary that runs it. Supported languages include shell, Python, Perl, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Expect, Tcl, AWK, JavaScript, Dart and AppleScript, or any user-specified interpreter. Generated apps can show progress bars, text output windows, WebKit HTML views, status menu items or droplets, and can accept dragged-and-dropped files or text as script arguments. Apps can be given their own icon, file type associations, identifier and version, and can optionally run scripts with root privileges, register as URI scheme handlers, send user notifications, or run in the background. A command line tool supports automation and build integration, and "profiles" save app configurations.
use_cases: Turn a shell or Python script into a double-clickable Mac app
Build installers, droplets or login items
Wrap scripts with a progress bar or output window GUI
Automate app bundle creation in build pipelines
how_to_run: Download Platypus 5.5.0 from the README's download link (macOS 11 or later)
To build from source: make build_unsigned (requires Xcode build tools)
The resulting application bundle is created in the products directory
CI command line tool install: unzip the release zip, cd Platypus.app/Contents/Resources, sudo bash InstallCommandLineTool.sh
notable: Wraps scripts in native .app bundles with a slim compiled launcher binary
Multiple interfaces: progress bar, text window, web view, status menu, droplet
Can run scripts with root privileges via the macOS Security Framework
Command line tool plus GUI, with saved profiles
Open source since around 2003 with a long release history
caveats: Requires macOS; the README targets macOS 11 or later
Building from source requires Xcode build tools
Author notes the early code has beginner-era structure and is not how he would write it today
keywords: drag and drop files to script
